title: Electrical Work Order Estimate Worksheet
subtitle: Residential Electrical Work: prices observed scope, options, and exclusions.
description: Electrical Work Order Estimate Worksheet covers branch circuit, panel position, device, conductor, load, and affected area. The electrical service coordinator records Residential Electrical Work observed scope, costs, options, and terms. Electrical Work Order Estimate Worksheet keeps Residential Electrical Work exceptions visible until the electrical service coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use Electrical Work Order Estimate Worksheet at residence, panel, circuit, room, device, and equipment connection. Document branch circuit, panel position, device, conductor, load, and affected area identity before Residential Electrical Work begins. Compare branch circuit, panel position, device, conductor, load, and affected area findings with stated Residential Electrical Work criteria; route unresolved Residential Electrical Work issues to qualified electrical reviewer. For Electrical Work Order Estimate Worksheet, confirm requirements for Residential Electrical Work. Ask qualified electrical reviewer to review Residential Electrical Work conditions beyond the electrical service coordinator's role.

sections.title: Property estimate review and customer identity
sections.guidance: Identify the customer, asset or property, estimator, and basis date before pricing the work.

blocks.label: Residential Electrical Work identity

fields.label: Panel, circuit, device, and load identifier
Reported trip, outage, heat, damage, or performance history

blocks.guidance: Use the Residential Electrical Work identifier printed on branch circuit, panel position, device, conductor, load, and affected area or its linked source record.

sections.title: Pricing options and customer decision inputs
sections.guidance: Price the observable work and options. Keep concealed conditions and unconfirmed quantities out of fixed scope.

blocks.label: Residential Electrical Work scope observations
items: De-energization and absence-of-voltage control within scope
Panel, breaker, conductor, termination, and enclosure condition
Device, receptacle, switch, fixture, and grounding observation
Load, rating, labeling, and overcurrent-protection match
Heat, odor, arcing, moisture, and physical-damage signs
blocks.guidance: Mark what was observed or supplied as estimate input; explain anything material that could not be inspected.

sections.title: Estimate exception and change conditions
sections.guidance: State what could change the price, timing, method, or scope before the customer or responsible party decides.

blocks.label: Do not proceed without control
blocks.guidance: Stop normal processing when energization, grounding, overcurrent, conductor, panel, or authorization concern remains. Protect branch circuit, panel position, device, conductor, load, and affected area; document the Residential Electrical Work notification and await qualified electrical reviewer direction.

blocks.label: Conditions that may require a revised estimate or specialist review
items: Service or panel condition outside authorization
Heat, arcing, damaged conductor, or moisture concern
Required permit or qualified authority unavailable
blocks.guidance: For Residential Electrical Work, identify affected branch circuit, panel position, device, conductor, load, and affected area scope; ask electrical service coordinator to document the Residential Electrical Work immediate control before continuing.

sections.title: Estimate decision and selected service scope
sections.guidance: Record the selected option and spending limit. Approval of an estimate authorizes only the stated scope and terms.

blocks.label: Estimate support retained
blocks.guidance: Attach or link proof for branch circuit, panel position, device, conductor, load, and affected area; mark only Residential Electrical Work evidence present in that record.
